chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his wife or to his slave girl, after he had shaved (his head), but had not performed Tawaf and had not performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa: 'Cast off your garment,' and he looked at her private parts. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him, if there was nothing other than looking.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: The two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'ee
key_terms.حَلَقَ: Shaving the head (one of the pillars of Hajj)
key_terms.سَعَى: Performing Sa'ee (walking between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who has sex with his wife after shaving but before completing Tawaf and Sa'ee?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between minor and major violations of Ihram prohibitions, specifically addressing the scenario where the pilgrim has already performed the initial shaving (Halq) but not the final Tawaf and Sa'i. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights that mere visual intimacy without full sexual intercourse does not incur the penalty of Dam (sacrifice), reflecting a nuanced application of the principle that penalties are tied to the specific prohibited act committed. This hadith is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Hilli and Al-Majlisi to distinguish between 'Nikah' (marital union) and 'Tamattu' (enjoyment) in the context of Hajj rituals.
